- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon; apply a 2–5% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending downward, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast mid-horizon.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast correction by 1–2 periods unless sentiment is strong and persistent.
